questions.q: What is food security, and what are its dimensions?
answer: Food security means that food is available, accessible and affordable to all people at all times.

answer.text: There must be enough food, whether produced within the country, imported, or held in government stocks.
The food must be within the physical reach of every person, in all regions.
People must have enough money to buy sufficient, safe and nutritious food to meet their needs.

Food security is threatened by calamities such as droughts and floods, by war, and by rising prices, and the poorest — landless labourers and casual workers — are the most vulnerable. A country is truly food-secure only when even the poorest can obtain enough food at all times.

questions.q: How does India ensure food security through the buffer stock and the Public Distribution System?
answer: After the Green Revolution made India self-sufficient in foodgrains, the government built a system to ensure food reaches everyone.

answer.text: The Food Corporation of India buys wheat and rice from farmers at a Minimum Support Price and stores them as a buffer stock. This stock is used to distribute food in deficit areas and to poorer households, and to steady prices in times of shortage.

The stock is distributed through the Public Distribution System, which supplies foodgrains at low prices through ration shops, or fair price shops, using ration cards such as the Antyodaya cards for the poorest families.
The National Food Security Act of 2013 made access to food a legal right for about two-thirds of the population.
